core_obligations: Rewrite one fibre product (proof lines 16551-16562): since K is separably closed, every etale K-algebra is a finite product of copies of K, so Spec(K) x_S Spec(O^{sh}_{S, sbar}) is a cofiltered limit of finite disjoint unions of copies of Spec(K), with nonempty index sets because a morphism Spec(K) -> Spec(O^{sh}_{S, sbar}) is given.

Rewrite the other fibre product (proof lines 16563-16576): consequently Spec(O^{sh}_{X, xbar}) x_S Spec(K) is the limit over the same index category of the disjoint unions of Spec(O^{sh}_{X, xbar}) x_{Spec(O^{sh}_{S, sbar})} Spec(K).

Apply commutation with limits (proof lines 16577-16578): since cohomology commutes with limits of schemes, the cohomology of the left hand side of the first formulation is the colimit of the cohomologies of the pieces, and the two formulations become equivalent.
proof_roadmap: Use that K is separably closed to write Spec(K) x_S Spec(O^{sh}_{S, sbar}) as a cofiltered limit of finite disjoint unions of copies of Spec(K).
Rewrite the fibre product defining the first formulation with the second strict henselian factor in place.
Use commutation of cohomology with limits to compare the two formulations term by term.
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that two ways of writing the base change comparison at a geometric point, one using the fibre product over S and one using the fibre product over Spec(O^{sh}_{S, sbar}), give the same cohomology (statement lines 16531-16548). The proof has one genuinely non-formal step: because K is separably closed, every etale K-algebra is a finite product of copies of K, so the fibre product Spec(K) x_S Spec(O^{sh}_{S, sbar}) is a cofiltered limit of finite disjoint unions of copies of Spec(K) (proof lines 16551-16562), after which the other fibre product inherits the same limit shape (proof lines 16563-16576) and commutation of cohomology with limits finishes the comparison (proof lines 16577-16578). The non-formal content is the limit description, which is why separably closedness of K is assumed. The claim is H2: one limit rewriting plus one standard commutation.
